      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "058706caa517c5de109520464c2a0bc9bce6d2f58f153cc675fcf01194607db0",
        "text": "**Why:** on 2026-08-05 one sentence in RE-call's `ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` asserting an\nintegrity check was wrong **four times**: a digest of the pre-rewrite script; a test-file digest\nthat moved when one test was appended; the CRLF/LF boundary above; and finally staleness inside its\nown commit. The first three corrections all patched the number. **Four rounds on one claim means\nthe mechanism is wrong, not the value**, and this was three rounds of treating a mechanism failure\nas an arithmetic one, in a document whose argument is that undemonstrated claims are the failure\nmode. The same class from the other side: a mutation harness whose `write_text` restore rewrote LF\nas CRLF and left ten files dirty with no content diff.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-working-copy-vs-git-blob-crlf-boundary-2026-08-05.md",
        "ordinal": 3,

        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "confidence": 0.679620039108006,

        "chunk_id": "aa28ce5b43aae822c5035488423733e75eb7b6d8a1ece56245f15858dcc92b29",
        "text": "Writing a literal U+2028 into a Python test file via the editing tools is unreliable. On\n2026-08-11, in `tests/test_fix.py`, the same pasted character survived in one test and was\nsilently turned into an ordinary space (U+0020) in two others written minutes later.\n\n**Why it matters more than it sounds:** the affected tests were guards ABOUT line separators. With\nthe separator flattened to a space, one guard passed against the unfixed code and another failed\nagainst the fixed code, that is, the results inverted. Nothing in the pytest output looked wrong;\nonly dumping the source's actual code points found it. This is [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] arriving\nthrough the editor rather than through the assertion.",

    "query": "why did writing a file with python change every line ending",

      {
        "chunk_id": "04fa29f55043a3f08b1186d2911e7960a056264d460a13b045961f1b0ce340c0",
        "text": "- Prefer the Edit tool for file changes; it does not do this.\n- If scripting an edit in Python, pass `newline=\"\\n\"`:\n  `path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\n\")`.\n- To diagnose: `git ls-files --eol <file>` shows index vs working-tree endings directly.\n- To confirm a diff is line-endings-only, hash both sides normalised rather than trusting\n  `git diff --ignore-all-space`, which also hides real whitespace changes:\n  `git show HEAD:f | tr -d '\\r' | sha256sum` against `tr -d '\\r' < f | sha256sum`.\n- To fix once content is confirmed identical: `git checkout -- <files>`. Do NOT commit it; the\n  commit would record no content change.\n\nRelated: [[ruff-blocked-locally]] for the other local tooling gotcha in this repo.",
        "source": "recall/python-write-text-crlf-churn.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.908049+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.615793989206077,
        "confidence": 0.9886639631811434,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c5c2a03b5b79f244f3efe8069a5992d87f4c6e6d774fb0a8ffaa23daa7f66083",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Same session, a second way a \"successful\" write leaves the wrong state, unrelated to concurrency.\r\nMy mutation harness restored each file with `path.write_text(original)` and verified the restore by\r\ncomparing a hash of `read_text`. It passed. `git status` still showed the file **modified**: on\r\nWindows `write_text` had converted the whole file **LF \u2192 CRLF**, and `read_text` universalises\r\nnewlines on read, so the hash could not see what the write had done. Had I committed, the diff would\r\nhave been every line of `recall/lineage.py`.\r\n\ud83d\udd11 **A hash taken through a normalising read cannot verify a write.** Verify a restore with\r\n`git diff --stat` (or `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` to separate content from endings), not with a\r\nchecksum you computed yourself. Same family as *diff the file",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24.md",
        "ordinal": 30,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:16.076122+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6109291315078779,
        "confidence": 0.9861403537114042,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eda6c34066b95c6fa7aaab16e2f773cf9abd7aecc5a6d38c408031b9e4aa71b7",
        "text": "This repo's `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`, so the working tree is meant to be LF\neven on Windows. `Path.write_text(...)` in Python's default text mode translates `\\n` to `\\r\\n`\non Windows, so any file edited that way comes back as CRLF and git reports it modified forever,\nwith `warning: CRLF will be replaced by LF` on every add.\n\nObserved 2026-08-07: after a session of scripted edits, `git status` showed `recall/retriever.py`\nand `recall/store.py` as modified with **zero content difference**. `git ls-files --eol` showed\n`i/lf w/crlf`, i.e. index LF, working tree CRLF.\n\n**How to apply:**",
        "source": "recall/python-write-text-crlf-churn.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.894091+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.600415110588078,
        "confidence": 0.9786453545907314,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "058706caa517c5de109520464c2a0bc9bce6d2f58f153cc675fcf01194607db0",
        "text": "**Why:** on 2026-08-05 one sentence in RE-call's `ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` asserting an\nintegrity check was wrong **four times**: a digest of the pre-rewrite script; a test-file digest\nthat moved when one test was appended; the CRLF/LF boundary above; and finally staleness inside its\nown commit. The first three corrections all patched the number. **Four rounds on one claim means\nthe mechanism is wrong, not the value**, and this was three rounds of treating a mechanism failure\nas an arithmetic one, in a document whose argument is that undemonstrated claims are the failure\nmode. The same class from the other side: a mutation harness whose `write_text` restore rewrote LF\nas CRLF and left ten files dirty with no content diff.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-working-copy-vs-git-blob-crlf-boundary-2026-08-05.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:23.606073+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5269734263420143,
        "confidence": 0.679620039108006,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "aa28ce5b43aae822c5035488423733e75eb7b6d8a1ece56245f15858dcc92b29",
        "text": "Writing a literal U+2028 into a Python test file via the editing tools is unreliable. On\n2026-08-11, in `tests/test_fix.py`, the same pasted character survived in one test and was\nsilently turned into an ordinary space (U+0020) in two others written minutes later.\n\n**Why it matters more than it sounds:** the affected tests were guards ABOUT line separators. With\nthe separator flattened to a space, one guard passed against the unfixed code and another failed\nagainst the fixed code, that is, the results inverted. Nothing in the pytest output looked wrong;\nonly dumping the source's actual code points found it. This is [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] arriving\nthrough the editor rather than through the assertion.",

        "text": "Measured 2026-08-16, by probing every server directly over MCP streamable HTTP\nrather than by opinion:\n\n- **All five internal servers are live and reachable** on the tailnet.\n  `qwen-mcp` is `qwen-agent 1.27.0` with **33 tools**.\n- `code_search`, `db_query_ro` and `rg_search_live` all returned correct results\n  **first try, with correct arguments**.         "text": "\u2705 **M2 COMPLETE 2026-07-07** (self-recall MCP loop). `recall_mcp` FastMCP server over stdio, 5 commits (365c78a\u2192c678017): `recall_search` (structured hits + `gap_warning` + actionable `advice` + staleness), `recall_index` (agent writes own memory), `recall_stats` (freshness/count), thin `recall_mcp/service.py` over the engine, lifespan-managed store+embedder, + `examples/self_recall_agent.py` (anti-re-litigation `decide()`). **32 tests pass, ruff clean; verified E2E** (real stdio MCP client listed 3 tools + called recall_stats OK). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-07-recall-m2-mcp.md`. \u26a0\ufe0f **Built INLINE, not subagent-driven** \u2014 the general-purpose subagents misfired repeatedly (delegation loops: spawned children + waited instead of implementing); switched to inline for reliability.",

        "text": "`code-rag` (8 tools), `qwen-mcp` (33), `qwen-vps3`, `vps3-lite` (10), `mcp-pg-ops` (38) all index\n`/opt/sentiment_agent` and query the `sentiment_agent` database. **`code_search` on those servers\ndoes not search recall, and `db_query_ro` does not reach recall's tables.** They are wired into\nrecall now because the user asked for them, but reaching for them to answer a question about this\nrepository returns confident answers about a different codebase. That is the failure mode to watch\nfor: not an error, a wrong corpus.\n\n## What was actually missing: recall did not dogfood itself\n\nrecall ships an MCP server (`recall_mcp`, 10 tools) and `docs/USING_WITH_CLAUDE.md` documents\nexactly how to install it. The project did not use it on itself. It does now:",
        "source": "recall/recall-mcp-servers-wrong-corpus.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:51.757942+00:00",

        "chunk_id": "66d2284d850ade5a443f519da30ba54fc0bfd788856239743aa7af7c6016631b",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-16, by probing every server directly over MCP streamable HTTP\nrather than by opinion:\n\n- **All five internal servers are live and reachable** on the tailnet.\n  `qwen-mcp` is `qwen-agent 1.27.0` with **33 tools**.\n- `code_search`, `db_query_ro` and `rg_search_live` all returned correct results\n  **first try, with correct arguments**. The documented 17.1% error rate is\n  caller error, confirmed rather than assumed.\n- **`.mcp.json` existed in 4 of 41 checkouts.** recall 3 of 21, sentiment-agent\n  **1 of 20**. So 37 of 41 sessions began with no MCP servers at all.",
        "source": "recall/mcp-servers-unused-because-absent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.223272+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5438215408431575,
        "confidence": 0.8110685363850341,
        "verdict": "ok",

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2af4f5e8887d726720410849e9d89d4d14bd7afdcf1a75ee0d8bc918013937cc",
        "text": "\u2705 **M2 COMPLETE 2026-07-07** (self-recall MCP loop). `recall_mcp` FastMCP server over stdio, 5 commits (365c78a\u2192c678017): `recall_search` (structured hits + `gap_warning` + actionable `advice` + staleness), `recall_index` (agent writes own memory), `recall_stats` (freshness/count), thin `recall_mcp/service.py` over the engine, lifespan-managed store+embedder, + `examples/self_recall_agent.py` (anti-re-litigation `decide()`). **32 tests pass, ruff clean; verified E2E** (real stdio MCP client listed 3 tools + called recall_stats OK). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-07-recall-m2-mcp.md`. \u26a0\ufe0f **Built INLINE, not subagent-driven** \u2014 the general-purpose subagents misfired repeatedly (delegation loops: spawned children + waited instead of implementing); switched to inline for reliability.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project_recall_public_rag_repo_2026-07-06.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:11.948576+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5647727769884137,

        "verdict": "ok",

      },
      {

        "text": "Until 2026-08-15 the recall project had **no MCP servers at all**: no `.mcp.json`, nothing under\n`mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`. The five internal servers were configured only for\n`progetto sentimental`, so recall sessions never had them. All five were reachable the whole time,\nwhich is why this looked like a working setup and was not.\n\n## They are reachable, and their corpus is not this repo",

        "text": "funder wallet): `post_exit_7d` is a lower bound, so a low ratio is confounded \u21d2 NEEDS_DATA not a false FAIL. A PASS re-arms nothing (lane closed #1804, maker halted `_RMK_KILL`).\n\n## 5. \u00a72b deadman checks (local scheduled tasks)\n`gate-check-1895-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1897-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1896-2026-08-06` \u2014 each runs the gate-check + posts the verdict (run when the app is open / next launch).",

        "text": "**Why:** CLAUDE.md \u00a72b makes every gate carry a scheduled check as its deadman, but there is no\ninverse rule. An orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident,\nself-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to\nre-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen. The scheduled task's own\nframing is stale data, not authority \u2014 [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]]\nis the same failure shape one layer down.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",

        "valid_from": null,

        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "87360cf238b9be73104d1ced608462149da32db54da70e47051274df296ecf84",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. On arming any probe, note the **terminal table** the gate query reads (e.g. `polymarket_live_orders`, `*_fills`) \u2014 not the signals or dry-ledger table.\n2. Within 24-48h, run `SELECT count(*), max(<ts>) FROM <terminal_table> WHERE <edge_id/slug filter> AND <ts> >= <arm_date>`. Zero rows \u21d2 **not armed** \u2014 fix or close, do not let it ride to the gate date.\n3. Sanity-check the whole `systemd-analyze cat-config` view of the unit, not just the base unit file \u2014 drop-ins (`*.d/*.conf`) override `Environment=`, and a later `EnvironmentFile=` can too ([[reference_systemd_environmentfile_overrides_environment_2026-07-12]]).\n4. Every gate issue must have a paired scheduled check (CLAUDE.md Session-Close \u00a72b). #1594 had none, which is why it drifted 13 days unnoticed.",

        "text": "Closing a `gate` issue early (lane death, venue repricing, moot verdict) leaves its paired\n`/schedule` deadman armed. On 2026-07-21 the `maker-net-tuner-gate-run` task fired for gate\n#1494 \u2014 closed 2026-07-16 with the LRP lane. The task instructions still read as a live gate\n(\"ahead of the 2026-07-21 gate\") and prescribed training + posting a learned-vs-baseline\nverdict.",

        "ordinal": 0,

        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Session-Close \u00a72c (gate resolved \u2192 comment + close) is incomplete: also **cancel or repoint\n  the paired scheduled check** in the same session.\n- When a scheduled gate task fires, **read the issue state FIRST**. `state: CLOSED` \u21d2 the correct\n  output is a SUPERSEDED note on the issue, not a run.\n- Do not treat \"the run is technically feasible\" as a reason to run. #1494's substrate was still\n  writing and the tuner still imported cleanly; the blocker was economic (`rewardsMinSize`\n  20\u2192200 priced us out), and no allocator result could move it.\n  See [[project-lrp-reward-farming-closed-venue-repricing-2026-07-16]] and\n  [[feedback-venue-can-reprice-you-out-overnight-2026-07-16]].",

        "text": "funder wallet): `post_exit_7d` is a lower bound, so a low ratio is confounded \u21d2 NEEDS_DATA not a false FAIL. A PASS re-arms nothing (lane closed #1804, maker halted `_RMK_KILL`).\n\n## 5. \u00a72b deadman checks (local scheduled tasks)\n`gate-check-1895-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1897-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1896-2026-08-06` \u2014 each runs the gate-check + posts the verdict (run when the app is open / next launch).",

      {
        "chunk_id": "b1e319607401c01d2645d5614aa5f0cbf541a9dab0967c4b83f5c0d1c62094b2",
        "text": "**Why:** CLAUDE.md \u00a72b makes every gate carry a scheduled check as its deadman, but there is no\ninverse rule. An orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident,\nself-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to\nre-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen. The scheduled task's own\nframing is stale data, not authority \u2014 [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]]\nis the same failure shape one layer down.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.866789+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "87360cf238b9be73104d1ced608462149da32db54da70e47051274df296ecf84",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. On arming any probe, note the **terminal table** the gate query reads (e.g. `polymarket_live_orders`, `*_fills`) \u2014 not the signals or dry-ledger table.\n2. Within 24-48h, run `SELECT count(*), max(<ts>) FROM <terminal_table> WHERE <edge_id/slug filter> AND <ts> >= <arm_date>`. Zero rows \u21d2 **not armed** \u2014 fix or close, do not let it ride to the gate date.\n3. Sanity-check the whole `systemd-analyze cat-config` view of the unit, not just the base unit file \u2014 drop-ins (`*.d/*.conf`) override `Environment=`, and a later `EnvironmentFile=` can too ([[reference_systemd_environmentfile_overrides_environment_2026-07-12]]).\n4. Every gate issue must have a paired scheduled check (CLAUDE.md Session-Close \u00a72b). #1594 had none, which is why it drifted 13 days unnoticed.",

        "valid_until": null,

      {

        "text": "Closing a `gate` issue early (lane death, venue repricing, moot verdict) leaves its paired\n`/schedule` deadman armed. On 2026-07-21 the `maker-net-tuner-gate-run` task fired for gate\n#1494 \u2014 closed 2026-07-16 with the LRP lane. The task instructions still read as a live gate\n(\"ahead of the 2026-07-21 gate\") and prescribed training + posting a learned-vs-baseline\nverdict.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 0,

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "e3c2c95967af3f2506d9a8d5867adf3d12d68c8a70c1f2d3197cf3308da501b5",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Session-Close \u00a72c (gate resolved \u2192 comment + close) is incomplete: also **cancel or repoint\n  the paired scheduled check** in the same session.\n- When a scheduled gate task fires, **read the issue state FIRST**. `state: CLOSED` \u21d2 the correct\n  output is a SUPERSEDED note on the issue, not a run.\n- Do not treat \"the run is technically feasible\" as a reason to run. #1494's substrate was still\n  writing and the tuner still imported cleanly; the blocker was economic (`rewardsMinSize`\n  20\u2192200 priced us out), and no allocator result could move it.\n  See [[project-lrp-reward-farming-closed-venue-repricing-2026-07-16]] and\n  [[feedback-venue-can-reprice-you-out-overnight-2026-07-16]].",

  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "7627a6144867fa9a52b6d8fe0e77256ee89910be74868c79b4592c375ce411ad",
        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.059120+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6086865793092942,
        "confidence": 0.9847976562062956,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.081384+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863803132033721,
        "confidence": 0.9622275154086811,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "recall/parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:46.823291+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5561231706215851,
        "confidence": 0.8777915308580624,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2f6cb48db80920615da9c06f55508b653f4a0caa7815ea4a2c884079d970dd36",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "recall/guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:42.710215+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5298556405219826,
        "confidence": 0.7052907687701772,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "7cccba84a63aff61faa5ebab8e33ae791b7c3f59f4b471028cf857fc54a7d386",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.809843+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5979035736379973,
        "confidence": 0.9763351431279611,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eec41629f616f5a2ff7265198388f4308798a1baca5e0f6cc67b3a0011974d1d",
        "text": "**Why:** [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] covers guards that never fire because the assertion was\nunsatisfiable or too narrow from the start. This is the adjacent failure: a guard that used to\nfire, and quietly stops, because it depends on a string/event contract nobody versioned. The\nguard-test in that memory (mutate and watch it go red) catches the first kind but not this one,\nbecause the mutation target is the code under test, not the upstream tool the gate depends on.",
        "source": "recall/verifier-canary-liveness.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:56.737372+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5897769859233787,
        "confidence": 0.9670669242347618,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "bac25f19474642109d42944aa9c0c4799192203d267492e8330b9ba8914a85bc",
        "text": "Un guard non \u00e8 finito quando i suoi controlli passano. \u00c8 finito quando la cosa che **restituisce**\nsoddisfa ancora quei controlli.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": null,

  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "7627a6144867fa9a52b6d8fe0e77256ee89910be74868c79b4592c375ce411ad",
        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.059120+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6086865793092942,
        "confidence": 0.9847976562062956,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.081384+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863803132033721,
        "confidence": 0.9622275154086811,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "recall/parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:46.823291+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5561231706215851,
        "confidence": 0.8777915308580624,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2f6cb48db80920615da9c06f55508b653f4a0caa7815ea4a2c884079d970dd36",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "recall/guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:42.710215+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5298556405219826,
        "confidence": 0.7052907687701772,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "7cccba84a63aff61faa5ebab8e33ae791b7c3f59f4b471028cf857fc54a7d386",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.809843+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5979035736379973,
        "confidence": 0.9763351431279611,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eec41629f616f5a2ff7265198388f4308798a1baca5e0f6cc67b3a0011974d1d",
        "text": "**Why:** [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] covers guards that never fire because the assertion was\nunsatisfiable or too narrow from the start. This is the adjacent failure: a guard that used to\nfire, and quietly stops, because it depends on a string/event contract nobody versioned. The\nguard-test in that memory (mutate and watch it go red) catches the first kind but not this one,\nbecause the mutation target is the code under test, not the upstream tool the gate depends on.",
        "source": "recall/verifier-canary-liveness.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:56.737372+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5897769859233787,
        "confidence": 0.9670669242347618,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "bac25f19474642109d42944aa9c0c4799192203d267492e8330b9ba8914a85bc",
        "text": "Un guard non \u00e8 finito quando i suoi controlli passano. \u00c8 finito quando la cosa che **restituisce**\nsoddisfa ancora quei controlli.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05.md",

Running the code is\n  normally the strongest evidence available; here it faithfully measured **the wrong tree**.\n- Three sibling clones exist (`~/Documents/RE-call`, `re-call`, `recall`) on different branches.\n  Picking one by name and finding a git repo is not picking the right one.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **Evidence quality does not survive a wrong substrate.** Verifying harder (running vs reading)\nmade the false finding *more* convincing, not less.",

        "text": "twice. Reacting to either at face value leads to re-doing landed work, or worse, force-pushing\r\nover it. This is the same family as [[feedback-check-head-vs-origin-before-reading-code-2026-07-24]]\r\n\u2014 a wrong picture of the tree \u2014 but the opposite direction: there the checkout was *behind* origin,\r\nhere",

        "text": "is a SNAPSHOT, and it rots inside the session\r\n\r\nThe hook that claims the workspace prints a line like `vs origin/master  0 behind, 0 ahead`. That is\r\nmeasured once, before the first turn. On a two-hour session it is stale by the time you commit.\r\n\r\nMeasured: the hook said **0 behind, 0 ahead**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",

        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",

        "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are). Previous workflow muscle memory (`sudo systemctl restart anything`, `cat .env`, `sudo psql`, `daemon-reload`) is broken by design and must not be reintroduced.",

        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",

        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell).         "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are).         "text": "## NON coperti (richiedono password sudo, NON eseguire autonomamente)\n\n- `apt`, `apt-get`, `apt install|update|upgrade|autoremove|clean` \u2014 install/cleanup pacchetti\n- `tee` verso path arbitrari (es. `/etc/sysctl.d/`, `/etc/logrotate.d/`) \u2014 solo `/etc/sentiment/healthcheck.url` \u00e8 coperto\n- `sysctl --system`, `sysctl -w` \u2014 tweak kernel\n- `tuned-adm profile *` \u2014 performance tuning\n- `logrotate` (esecuzione + config write)\n- `usermod`, `gpasswd`, `passwd root` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (negate, mai concessi)\n- `visudo` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` negate\n- `cat /root/age/*` e variants \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (age key protection)\n- `docker` per container fuori dal set monitoring (no general `docker exec`, `docker run`, `docker build`)\n\n## Implicazioni operative",
